# Aurora, the full documentation

> Aurora is a macOS Tahoe-inspired desktop theme for KDE Plasma 6 on CachyOS and other Arch-based systems. It adds a menu bar, a Dock, Quick Menu, a Control Center, notification banners, a Finder-style file manager and glass window buttons, keeps the shortcuts people know from Windows, and installs and uninstalls with one command.

---

Source: README.md (README)

(Picture: Aurora: a macOS Tahoe-inspired desktop for CachyOS and KDE Plasma 6. Developed by xt0n1.)

## Overview

Aurora is a macOS Tahoe-inspired theme for KDE Plasma 6 on CachyOS. It is not a copy of Tahoe: it takes its look and its ideas and fits them to Plasma. You get a menu bar at the top, a Dock at the bottom, Quick Menu, the Control Center, notification banners, a Finder-style file manager and glass window buttons.

I moved from Windows 11 to CachyOS and wanted Tahoe's look without relearning my habits. So the Windows key opens Quick Menu, Win+E opens File Explorer, the window buttons are in Windows order (minimize, maximize, close) and menus show shortcuts as `Ctrl+C`.

One command installs it and one removes it. The installer saves every setting before it changes it, and `aurora uninstall` puts them back.

Nothing in KWin is patched and no file that belongs to a package is edited. Some parts are Plasma's own code rebuilt with a small patch, some are plugins that load ahead of the stock ones, some are Plasma widgets, and the rest are settings. When a system update brings a new Plasma, KWin or Qt, the parts built for the old version are skipped at login and Plasma uses its own until you rebuild them.

## Showcase

(Picture: The desktop: the menu bar with the CachyOS logo, the tray, Quick Menu, Control Center and the clock; File Explorer on the left; the Dock at the bottom; Dawn Bird, Aurora's wallpaper, a bird of folded glass rising on the right)

File Explorer, the menu bar and the Dock on Dawn Bird, Aurora's own wallpaper (KDE Plasma 6.8.2, CachyOS).

(Picture: Quick Menu: a frosted glass panel with the search field, Suggestions and the apps in sections)
Quick Menu opens on the Windows key. Right-click an app to pin it to the top or to the Dock, or to take it out of Suggestions. Drag apps to reorder them inside a category.
(Picture: Control Center: glass modules for Ethernet, Bluetooth, the player, Night Light, Focus and sound)
The Control Center, opened from the switch icon in the menu bar.

(Picture: The menu open under the CachyOS logo, with About This Computer, System Settings, Sleep, Restart, Shut Down, Lock Screen and Log Out)
CachyOS's logo takes the Apple logo's place. Its settings offer Arch Linux, Apple and Kali Linux too.
(Picture: Two notification banners in the bottom-right corner, one with Later and Install buttons)
Notifications arrive as banners in the bottom-right corner.

(Picture: The notifications popover under the bell: Do not disturb, then each notification on its own glass card with the app's icon, a bold title, the message and a picture)
The bell opens the notifications you missed, each on its own glass card as in macOS Tahoe.
(Picture: Mission Center on Performance: the device sidebar on clearer glass, the CPU graphs as tinted cards and its readings as glass tiles)
Mission Center in File Explorer's glass, with each app's GPU, memory and network counted exactly.

(Picture: Mission Center on Apps: the running apps and processes on a glass card, busy cells tinted warmer as they rise)
Apps and processes as in the Windows 11 Task Manager, with busy values tinted warmer as they rise.

## Features

| Part | What it does | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| File Explorer | A Finder-style file manager built on Dolphin. Click any folder of the path, drop files on it or drag it out; type a path (Ctrl+L) with suggestions and Tab; search the whole PC as you type from an index that runs only while File Explorer is used; press Space for Quick Look, F3 for Split View, and tag files with Finder's colors. The sidebar lists your drives with their free space, unfolds your folders and lists each tag's files. Win+E opens it, every app's Open and Save dialogs use it, and "Show in folder" opens it. | [`components/file-explorer`](components/file-explorer) |
| Window buttons | A glass capsule with minimize, maximize and close, in that order. Qt, GTK and libadwaita apps all get the same buttons at the same size. | [`components/window-buttons`](components/window-buttons) |
| Menu bar | The system menu under CachyOS's logo (or Arch Linux's, Apple's or Kali Linux's), the name of the active app, the tray, Quick Menu, Control Center and the clock, spaced the way macOS spaces them. There is no global menu. | [`components/kali-menu`](components/kali-menu), [`components/clock`](components/clock), [`themes/panels`](themes/panels) |
| System tray | Plasma's tray, with drag and drop like Windows 11: drag an icon to move it, or drop it on the arrow to hide it. | [`components/system-tray`](components/system-tray) |
| Quick Menu | The Windows key opens Tahoe's Applications view: the apps you use most, then every app by category. Right-click an app (or press the Menu key) to pin it to the top or to the Dock, or to take it out of Suggestions. Drag an app onto another one in the same category to move it there; the order is kept. All Applications lists every app by letter. Start typing to search with KRunner. The rail at the bottom works like Windows 11's Start: your picture and name open Lock, Switch User and Log Out, and the power button opens Sleep, Restart and Shut Down. | [`components/quick-menu`](components/quick-menu), [`components/windows-key`](components/windows-key) |
| Control Center | Network, Bluetooth, Focus, sound and its output devices, the player, Night Light, screen mirroring, settings and screenshots. | [`components/control-center`](components/control-center), [`components/glass`](components/glass) |
| Notifications | Banners with the app icon, a bold title, the text and the action buttons, in the bottom-right corner. The bell in the menu bar lists what you missed on glass cards, with Do not disturb at the top. | [`components/notifications`](components/notifications) |
| Dock | Your pinned apps, a divider, Downloads and Trash. It moves out of the way of windows that reach it; touch the bottom edge to bring it back. | [`components/dock-divider`](components/dock-divider), [`themes/panels`](themes/panels) |
| Animations | Windows open, close and minimize into the Dock the way macOS does it, at Plasma's designed speed; `aurora settings` makes them faster or turns them off. | [`components/motion`](components/motion) |
| Pointer | macOS cursors, and a pointing hand over anything you can click, KWin's window buttons included. | [`components/pointing-hand`](components/pointing-hand), [`themes/cursors`](themes/cursors) |
| Mission Center | Optional, with `aurora mission-center on`: Mission Center in File Explorer's glass, with each app's GPU, memory and network counted exactly, a lean background service and a color per device. Apps and Services read like the Windows 11 Task Manager. | [`components/mission-center`](components/mission-center) |
| Energy page | A page in Info Center that shows the CPU and GPU power draw, a two-minute chart and the power profiles. | [`components/energy-page`](components/energy-page) |
| Themes | Dawn Bird, Aurora's own wallpaper; Aurora's colors, Plasma style, Kvantum and GTK themes, cursors and icons with each app's own logo, the Inter font (or SF Pro, if you installed it) and a Konsole profile. | [`themes`](themes) |

## Requirements

| | |
| --- | --- |
| System | CachyOS, or another Arch-based distribution with pacman |
| Processor | Any 64-bit x86 processor (x86-64), old or new |
| Desktop | KDE Plasma 6 on Wayland. Tested on Plasma 6.8.2, KWin 6.8.2 and Qt 6.12.0. |
| Disk | About 700 MB for the build: the `build/` folder of a checkout, or `~/.cache/aurora/build` with the package |
| Time | Under a minute with the package, which comes with its parts built; about 3 minutes from the source, which builds them |

## Installation

One command, as yourself (not with sudo), in bash, zsh or fish:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xt0n1-t3ch/Aurora-CachyOS-Theme/main/get.sh | bash
```

It adds Aurora's signed pacman repository, installs the `aurora-theme` package and opens `aurora install`. The only question is which logo goes in the menu bar. Your password is asked once. Log out and back in when it finishes.

(Picture: What happens after you press Enter, in six steps: one command, already built, one question, backup, look, log in again.)

From then on, everything goes through the `aurora` command. Run it alone for a menu, or name what you want:

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `aurora` | A menu with everything below |
| `aurora install` | The guided install; `--logo`, `--colors`, `--performance` and `--yes` answer its questions up front |
| `aurora update` | Installs a new Aurora the safe way: with your system update when it is built for it, alone when it is built for your system as it is, not at all otherwise |
| `aurora rebuild` | Builds Aurora's parts again after a Plasma, KWin or Qt update |
| `aurora settings` | Update notices, animations, the menu bar logo, icons, performance tuning and Mission Center, in one menu |
| `aurora logo arch` | Changes the menu bar logo: `cachyos`, `arch`, `apple` or `kali`; `--colors` shows it in its own colors |
| `aurora icons breeze` | Changes the icon theme: `aurora` or any installed one; without a name it lists them |
| `aurora performance on` | Turns the measured tuning on or `off`; without a word it shows the four settings and asks |
| `aurora backups` | Lists the backups of your desktop from before Aurora; `aurora backups restore` puts one back |
| `aurora mission-center on` | Puts Aurora's Mission Center (exact per-app GPU, memory and network) in place of the distribution's, or `off`; `settings`, `snapshots` and `rollback` too |
| `aurora check-updates` | Looks for a newer Aurora right away |
| `aurora status` | What is installed, from where, whether Aurora's repository is set up, the tuning, and whether a rebuild is due |
| `aurora uninstall` | Puts your desktop back the way it was |

Aurora also tells you when a new version is out: a notification with **Update now** and **Skip this version**, once a day or on the schedule you pick in `aurora settings`.

<details>
<summary>What the one command does</summary>

[`get.sh`](get.sh) runs these steps; the first two happen once.

1. Trusts Aurora's signing key, [`aurora.asc`](packaging/repo/aurora.asc) (`657D 8110 799A 4E65 BE4E 1AB4 F028 2841 1279 4CC2`), after checking that the downloaded key has that fingerprint.
2. Adds the `[aurora]` section to `/etc/pacman.conf`. The repository is this project's [`repo` release](https://github.com/xt0n1-t3ch/Aurora-CachyOS-Theme/releases/tag/repo), and every file in it is signed.
3. Upgrades the system with the package, `sudo pacman -Syu aurora-theme`. The package brings every part already built, so nothing is compiled on your machine.
4. Opens `aurora install`, which saves your current settings to `~/.local/state/aurora/backups/`, applies the theme and keeps a log in `~/.local/state/aurora/logs`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Installing from the source instead</summary>

```bash
git clone https://github.com/xt0n1-t3ch/Aurora-CachyOS-Theme.git
cd Aurora-CachyOS-Theme
./install.sh
```

The script installs the packages it needs, builds the parts for your version of Plasma, saves your current settings and applies the theme. It installs the `aurora` command too when Rust is installed, and from then on the commands above work the same. Every [release](https://github.com/xt0n1-t3ch/Aurora-CachyOS-Theme/releases) also has an `aurora-X.Y.Z.tar.gz` to install without git. `./install.sh --help` lists its options.

</details>

<details>
<summary>What changes outside your home folder</summary>

| Path | Why | Removed by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/usr/lib/qt6/plugins/org.kde.kdecoration3/org.aurora.decoration.so` | A link to the window buttons in your home folder, since KWin loads decorations before your session starts | `aurora uninstall` |
| `/usr/lib/qt6/plugins/kwin/plugins/aurora-pointer.so` | A link to the pointing hand for window buttons, for the same reason | `aurora uninstall` |
| `/etc/scx_loader.toml`, `/etc/tmpfiles.d/thp.conf`, `/etc/sysctl.d/99-aurora-memory.conf`, `/etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf.d/90-aurora-zram.conf` | Only with the performance tuning | `aurora performance off` or `aurora uninstall` |

Everything else goes in your home folder. [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) has the full list.

</details>

## Keyboard shortcuts

| Keys | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Win</kbd> | Opens Quick Menu. Press it again or <kbd>Esc</kbd> to close it. |
| <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>Space</kbd> | Also opens Quick Menu |
| <kbd>Win</kbd>+<kbd>E</kbd> | Opens File Explorer |
| <kbd>Win</kbd>+<kbd>L</kbd> | Locks the screen (Plasma's default) |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>Del</kbd> | Opens the log out screen (Plasma's default) |

All of Plasma's other shortcuts work as before. Menus write them the Windows way, like `Ctrl+C`, not with Mac symbols.

## Updating

### A new version of Aurora

```bash
aurora update
```

It updates your system and the `aurora-theme` package together (through paru or yay if you have one, else `sudo pacman -Syu`), then installs the new version. It keeps your backup, your logo, your menu bar, your Dock and the tuning. From a source copy it pulls the newest commits instead. [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) lists what changed in each version.

### After a system update

The system tray, the notifications, Quick Menu and the window buttons are compiled for the exact versions of Plasma, KDecoration and Qt you have. If an update changes one of them, those parts are set aside at the next login and Plasma's own versions load instead. Nothing breaks; those parts look like stock Plasma until you rebuild them:

```bash
aurora rebuild
```

Then log out and back in. `aurora status` says whether a rebuild is due. If a new Plasma changes the lines a patch touches, [docs/update.md](docs/update.md) explains how to port it.

## Performance tuning

```bash
aurora performance on     # and off to go back to CachyOS's settings
```

Four system settings, each measured on a Ryzen 7 5800X with 32 GB of RAM before I kept it. They are optional; `aurora performance` alone shows whether they are on and asks, and `aurora install --performance` adds them during the install.

| Setting | What I measured |
| --- | --- |
| scx_lavd CPU scheduler, Auto mode | With 32 busy threads in the background, the emoji picker opened in 666 ms instead of 1099 ms and Konsole in 674 ms instead of 819 ms. 7-Zip scored 101k to 108k MIPS instead of 96k to 97k. |
| `vm.watermark_scale_factor = 125` | Direct-reclaim stalls dropped from about 1,560 every 15 minutes to zero. It keeps about 400 MB free. |
| lz4 compression for zram | Swapped-out pages load 2.8 times faster: 3.7 GB/s instead of 1.3 GB/s. It starts at the next boot. |
| Transparent huge pages set to `defer` | Huge pages are put together in the background instead of making the app wait. Before the change I counted 279,000 of those waits. |

[docs/performance.md](docs/performance.md) has the numbers, the scripts that produced them, and what I tried and dropped.

## Removal

```bash
aurora uninstall
```

This removes everything Aurora installed and puts back every setting the install saved before changing it: colors, icons, fonts, panels, shortcuts, window buttons, Quick Menu, the default file manager, the two links and the tuning. Log out and back in afterwards.

The backup stays in `~/.local/state/aurora/backups/`. `aurora backups` lists what is there and when each was taken, and `aurora backups restore NAME` puts a particular one back. From a source copy, `./uninstall.sh` does the same as `aurora uninstall`.

## Project structure

```text
get.sh          the one-command install: the pacman repository, the package, then aurora
install.sh      installs Aurora: packages, build, backup, files, look
uninstall.sh    restores the desktop from the backup install.sh made
LICENSE         the GNU GPL version 3
NOTICE.md       the attribution terms, and which license covers each part
CHANGELOG.md    what changed in each version
CITATION.cff    how to credit Aurora (GitHub's "Cite this repository")
llms.txt        a map of these documents for coding agents (llms-full.txt: all of them)
components/     one folder per part: file-explorer, window-buttons, quick-menu,
                system-tray, notifications, control-center, kali-menu, clock,
                dock-divider, glass, pointing-hand, energy-page, windows-key
cli/            the aurora command (Rust)
themes/         Dawn Bird (the wallpaper), icons, cursors, fonts, GTK, Konsole,
                and the menu bar and Dock layout
installer/      build.sh, install.py, the package list, session files, desktop entries
packaging/      the package aurora-theme and the repository's key
performance/    the optional system tuning, and the scripts that measured it
scripts/        check.sh runs every test; release.sh makes a release; the license,
                llms.txt and GitHub metadata tools
tests/          installer and release tests, and a sandbox that runs Plasma in a window
docs/           how each part works, and how to build, update, restore, test and release
assets/         the logo, the pictures on this page and the social preview
```

## Development

Start with [docs/index.md](docs/index.md) for how each part works, and [tests/index.md](tests/index.md) for the tests. Coding agents and language models can start from [llms.txt](llms.txt), the map of these documents, or read all of them at once in [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt).

```bash
installer/build.sh            # build every part into build/
scripts/check.sh              # build, then run every test (about 25 seconds after a build)
python3 -I scripts/llms.py    # write llms.txt and llms-full.txt again after a change to the docs
tests/sandbox/run.sh "$PWD/tests/sandbox/scenarios/quick-menu.sh" 120   # one scenario in a nested Plasma
```

Versions follow [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html), the changelog follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/2.0.0/), and commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/). To make a release, run `scripts/release.sh 1.2.0`. It runs the checks, dates the changelog, tags `v1.2.0` and builds the archive with its notes and checksums. [docs/releasing.md](docs/releasing.md) has the details.

## FAQ

### Will a Plasma update break my desktop?

No. Each compiled part records the versions it was built for. At login, a part built for different versions is skipped and Plasma loads its own instead; Quick Menu falls back to the stock KRunner. Run `aurora rebuild` to get Aurora's parts back.

### Does it change system files?

It adds two symbolic links in `/usr/lib/qt6/plugins`, and four files in `/etc` if you turn on the performance tuning. It doesn't edit any file that belongs to a package, and `aurora uninstall` removes all of them.

### Can I use Apple's SF Pro font?

Yes. Aurora ships only free fonts, because Apple's license doesn't allow SF Pro to be redistributed. Install it yourself (for example `paru -S apple-fonts`, which downloads it from Apple) and run `aurora update` again: when SF Pro or SF Mono with Nerd Fonts' symbols is installed, Aurora uses it instead of Inter and JetBrains Mono.

### Do I keep my wallpaper and pinned apps?

Yes. Your wallpaper stays; Dawn Bird, Aurora's own wallpaper, is only added to the list. Apps pinned to your task manager move to the Dock, after File Explorer.

### Does it work on X11?

I only use and test it on Wayland, which is CachyOS's default. X11 is untested.

### Can I try it without touching my desktop?

Yes. [`tests/sandbox`](tests/sandbox) runs a full Plasma session inside a window with its own home folder. [docs/sandbox.md](docs/sandbox.md) explains how to use it.

# Installing

The package installs Aurora with its parts built (README.md, [Installation](../README.md#installation)). From the
source:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/xt0n1-t3ch/Aurora-CachyOS-Theme.git
cd Aurora-CachyOS-Theme
./install.sh
```

Log out and back in once afterwards. `./install.sh --help` lists the options; the README explains them
([Install](../README.md#installation)).

## What each step runs

| Step | Runs | Changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Packages | `pacman -S --needed` with what `installer/dependencies.txt` lists and the system lacks, plus `installer/build-dependencies.txt` when the parts are built here | system packages (sudo) |
| 2. Themes | checks that `themes/` holds every theme | nothing |
| 3. Build | `installer/build.sh` ([build.md](build.md)); with the package, `installer/build.sh --current` checks its `prebuilt/` parts instead | `build/` (nothing with the package) |
| 4. Install | `installer/install.py backup`, then `files` (`components` with `--rebuild`) | the home folder |
| 5. System | links the window buttons and the pointing hand into `/usr/lib/qt6/plugins`; with `--performance`, the tuning files | sudo |
| 6. Look and panels | `installer/install.py look`, then `panels` (skipped with `--rebuild`) | settings, panels |

The steps of `installer/install.py` can run alone too:

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `install.py backup` | Saves every setting in `SAVED` to `~/.local/state/aurora/backups/<date>/home/`, lists in `created.txt` what does not exist yet, writes `restore.sh` and `windows_key.py` there and points `latest-backup` at it. Kept from the first install: a second run leaves it alone. |
| `install.py files` | Icon themes, cursors, color scheme, Plasma style, Kvantum, wallpapers, widgets, the built parts, desktop entries, Konsole files, the login script, the drop-ins, the D-Bus services, the portal, `rebuild.sh` and the `source` link |
| `install.py components` | Only the built parts, each beside what it was built for |
| `install.py look` | Fonts, units, colors, Plasma style, icons, cursor, Kvantum, notification corner, GTK, Konsole, decoration, Dock edge, the Windows key, Win+E, File Explorer as the default file manager |
| `install.py panels [--force]` | The menu bar and the Dock from `themes/panels/layout.js`, unless the menu bar is already there; then the tray settings and hidden items, and a plasmashell restart |
| `install.py check` | Lists what the steps need and cannot find; changes nothing |

`--no-session` installs files without telling the running Plasma session (the tests use it with a temporary HOME).

## Root steps by hand

`install.sh` runs these through sudo (with `SUDO_ASKPASS` set it uses `sudo -A`, a graphical password prompt):

```bash
P=~/.local/lib/qt6/plugins
sudo ln -sfn $P/org.kde.kdecoration3/org.aurora.decoration.so /usr/lib/qt6/plugins/org.kde.kdecoration3/
sudo ln -sfn $P/kwin/plugins/aurora-pointer.so /usr/lib/qt6/plugins/kwin/plugins/
qdbus6 org.kde.KWin /Plugins org.kde.KWin.Plugins.LoadPlugin aurora-pointer
# The tuning (aurora performance on, or --performance; performance/system/, reasons in performance.md):
sudo install -Dm644 performance/system/scx_loader.toml /etc/scx_loader.toml && sudo systemctl enable --now scx_loader.service
sudo install -Dm644 performance/system/thp.conf /etc/tmpfiles.d/thp.conf
sudo install -Dm644 performance/system/99-aurora-memory.conf /etc/sysctl.d/99-aurora-memory.conf && sudo sysctl -q --system
sudo install -Dm644 performance/system/90-aurora-zram.conf /etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf.d/90-aurora-zram.conf
```

## Checking an install

- `systemctl --user show -p MainPID --value plasma-krunner.service` runs `~/.local/lib/aurora/quick-menu/krunner`.
- `python3 -I components/windows-key/windows_key.py status` names `org.kde.krunner.desktop / _launch`.
- `qdbus6 org.kde.KWin /KWin supportInformation | grep -A1 ^Decoration` shows `Plugin: org.aurora.decoration`.
- `find ~/.local/lib/qt6/plugins -name '*.paused'` prints nothing (no part stepped aside).
- With `--performance`: `cat /sys/kernel/sched_ext/root/ops` names lavd; `cat /proc/sys/vm/watermark_scale_factor` is 125.

# Updates

## New versions of Aurora

Each release is built once, on the maintainer's machine, by `scripts/release.sh X.Y.Z --publish`: the package with
every part built goes into the signed pacman repository (the GitHub release named `repo`), so no user compiles
anything. pacman brings it with the rest of the system (`sudo pacman -Syu`), or `aurora update` brings it the safe
way described below.

Aurora also says when one is out. `aurora-updates.timer`, a user timer the install enables in
`~/.config/systemd/user`, runs `aurora check-updates --notify` once a day (and at the next login when the PC was off).
That looks in pacman's repositories with `checkupdates` (its own copy of the databases in `~/.cache/aurora/checkup-db`,
no root) and, when a newer aurora-theme is there, shows a notification. Only a new aurora-theme does: updates of
any other package never show it. Its buttons:

| Button | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Update now | Konsole opens with `aurora update` |
| Skip this version | no notice offers that version again; the next one is offered |
| (closed) | it asks again at the next check |

`aurora settings` chooses how often it looks: every day (the default), every week or never
(`aurora settings --updates weekly` from a script). The choice is in `~/.config/aurora/aurora.conf`; what the last
look found is in `~/.local/state/aurora/updates`. `aurora` looks again when its menu opens, unless it looked in the
last 5 minutes (a look takes about 4 s), and names a found version above the menu only while it is newer than the
installed one, by pacman's own `vercmp`: after an update through pacman or paru, the noted version is forgotten
instead of being offered again. Without a network the menu uses the last look. `aurora check-updates` looks right
away.

## How `aurora update` installs it

First it checks Aurora's repository on this PC, without root: pacman.conf's `[aurora]` section must point at
Aurora's address and pacman must trust Aurora's key, as [get.sh](../get.sh) sets them up. A missing section, one
left with an older address or without one, a removed key or one never signed: each is named, and with one password
`aurora update` puts it back the way get.sh does (the key travels inside `aurora`, with the fingerprint get.sh
checks). Without the section pacman would never see a new Aurora, and would even count the installed one as built
from the AUR. `aurora status` shows the repository's state.

`aurora update` changes nothing when no newer aurora-theme is out. When one is, it reads what that package was built
for before installing anything: pacman packages begin with a `.BUILDINFO` file that lists the packages of the machine
that built them, so it downloads only the first mebibyte of the package (the first 128 KiB held all of 1.1.1's). It
compares those versions with this PC the way the login script compares the parts' stamps: KDE Plasma, KWin and Qt
whole, KDecoration by its minor version.

| The new package is built for | `aurora update` runs | What changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| what a system update brings | `sudo pacman -Syu --needed aurora-theme` | Aurora and the rest of the system together, as Arch expects |
| this PC as it is, while a system update would bring another Plasma, KWin, Qt or KDecoration | `sudo pacman -U` with the package's address | only Aurora; the system update waits for Aurora's next build |
| neither | nothing | it names the versions that differ and how to update the system anyway |

When pacman ends, `aurora update` checks that the installed aurora-theme is the version it found; when it is not (a
mirror behind, a package held back), it says so and how to retry, instead of installing the older one again.

pacman checks the package's signature in every case: `pacman -U` with an address takes pacman.conf's `SigLevel`
unless `RemoteFileSigLevel` says otherwise. An aurora-theme built from the AUR is in no repository, so its AUR helper
updates it with the whole system, as before.

# After a system update

CachyOS updates with `sudo pacman -Syu` (or `paru`). The theme's compiled parts are built for the installed Plasma,
KWin, KDecoration and Qt. When those change, each part steps aside by itself and the stock component takes over:

| Changed package | What happens until the rebuild |
| --- | --- |
| plasma-workspace or qt6-base | at login the tray and the notifications applet are renamed `*.paused` and Plasma loads its own; Quick Menu's launcher starts `/usr/bin/krunner` |
| kdecoration | the window buttons are paused at login; KWin uses Breeze |
| kwin | KWin refuses the pointer plugin (no hand over window buttons) |

Nothing breaks; the desktop only loses the theme's look of those parts. To bring them back:

```bash
~/.local/share/aurora/rebuild.sh      # runs ./install.sh --rebuild in the checkout; then log out and in
```

It checks the packages, builds every part for the new versions ([build.md](build.md)), installs the built parts
beside what they were built for, refreshes the root links and loads the pointer plugin. Settings and panels stay as
they are.

## When a patch no longer applies

`build.sh` builds a Plasma part for a new Plasma version from that version's own sources with the part's patch. If the
new Plasma changed the same lines, the patch fails, the part is skipped and Plasma keeps its own. To port it:

1. Fetch the new upstream files into `components/<part>/upstream/` (the same sparse clone as `build.sh`, folders in its
   `sparse_paths`).
2. Port `vendor/` onto them: keep the theme's changes (they are marked `Aurora:` in comments) and take every
   upstream change. Update the version in the component's `project(... VERSION ...)`.
3. Regenerate the patch as the difference from `upstream/` to `vendor/` (`diff -ruN` of two copies named `a` and `b`,
   leaving out the binary `*.qsb`), then check that `patch -p1` on a fresh copy of `upstream/`, plus the `.qsb`,
   reproduces `vendor/` exactly.
4. Run the part's tests and sandbox scenario, then `installer/build.sh <part>` and `install.py components`.

## The themes

Aurora's themes live in `themes/` and change like any other file: edit, reinstall what the install copies
(`install.py files`), test in the sandbox, commit. The base icons are a built archive
(`themes/icons/base/Aurora-base.tar.xz`, made reproducibly with `tar --sort=name --mtime`).

## A new Plasma for the package

The aurora-theme package carries its parts built for one Plasma, KWin and Qt. When Arch or CachyOS ships a new one,
raise `pkgrel` in `packaging/aur/PKGBUILD`, build the package again on an up-to-date machine and publish it to the
pacman repository ([releasing.md](releasing.md)); until then, each user's login script sets aside the parts built for
the older version and Plasma uses its own, and `aurora rebuild` builds them for a user who does not want to wait.

Source: docs/restore.md (Removal)

[Aurora](../README.md) / [Documentation](index.md) / Restore

# Going back

## Everything: `aurora uninstall`

`aurora uninstall` (or `./uninstall.sh` in a source copy) runs `restore.sh` in the backup that `~/.local/state/aurora/latest-backup` names, the one the first install
made. The restore stops plasmashell, deletes every path in `created.txt`, puts back every saved setting from `home/`,
unsets the session environment, gives Win+E back to Dolphin and the Windows key back to Plasma's launcher (with the
`windows_key.py` saved beside it), reloads D-Bus and the portal, restarts KRunner as Plasma ships it, removes the two
plugin links and, when present, the performance tuning (one password prompt each), puts the notification corner and
the GTK theme back, and starts plasmashell. Log out and back in afterwards. The backup stays where it is.
`aurora backups` lists the backups with the time each was taken and how many settings it saved, and
`aurora backups restore NAME` runs the `restore.sh` of another one.

## One part at a time

| Part | Undo |
| --- | --- |
| Quick Menu | `rm ~/.config/systemd/user/plasma-krunner.service.d/aurora.conf && systemctl --user daemon-reload && systemctl --user restart plasma-krunner.service` |
| Windows key | `python3 -I components/windows-key/windows_key.py stock` |
| Notification banners | `mv ~/.local/lib/qt6/plugins/plasma/applets/org.kde.plasma.notifications.so{,.paused}`, then restart plasmashell |
| Notification corner | `kwriteconfig6 --file plasmanotifyrc --group Notifications --key PopupPosition --delete` |
| System tray | `mv ~/.local/lib/qt6/plugins/plasma/applets/org.kde.plasma.systemtray.so{,.paused}`, then restart plasmashell |
| Window buttons | System Settings > Colors & Themes > Window Decorations > Breeze |
| CPU scheduler | `sudo systemctl disable --now scx_loader.service` |
| Memory tuning | `sudo rm /etc/sysctl.d/99-aurora-memory.conf /etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf.d/90-aurora-zram.conf && sudo sysctl -w vm.watermark_scale_factor=10` |

A new part means a new entry in `ADDED` or `SAVED` and, when it needs more than deleting files, a line in the
`RESTORE` template of `installer/install.py`.

# How the theme hooks into the desktop

The theme never edits a file that a package owns. Each part either loads ahead of the stock component with the same
id, is started instead of it through a user-level systemd drop-in, or is a setting that `installer/install.py`
writes after saving the old value. Root is needed for two plugin links, and for the tuning only with `--performance`.

## Session start

`~/.config/plasma-workspace/env/aurora.sh` (from [`installer/session/aurora.sh`](../installer/session/aurora.sh))
is sourced by Plasma before KWin and plasmashell start. It:

- puts `~/.local/lib/qt6/plugins` first in `QT_PLUGIN_PATH` and `~/.local/lib/qt6/qml` first in `QML_IMPORT_PATH`;
- sets `PLASMA_INTEGRATION_USE_PORTAL=1` and `GTK_USE_PORTAL=1`, so Open and Save panels come from File Explorer;
- compares what each plugin was built for with the installed packages, and renames a plugin built for other versions
  to `*.paused`, so Plasma and KWin load their stock part instead of one built for other libraries.

| In `~/.local/share/aurora/` | Holds | Guards |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `system-tray-built-for` | plasma-workspace and qt6-base versions | the system tray |
| `notifications-built-for` | plasma-workspace and qt6-base versions | the notifications applet |
| `window-buttons-built-for` | kdecoration major.minor | the window decoration |
| `quick-menu-built-for` | plasma-workspace and qt6-base versions | Quick Menu (checked by its launcher at every start) |

`installer/build.sh` writes `build/<part>/built-for`; the install copies it beside the installed part, and
`~/.local/share/aurora/rebuild.sh` builds and installs again ([update.md](update.md)).

## Plugins that load ahead of the stock ones

Same plugin id, found first through `QT_PLUGIN_PATH` (KPluginMetaData prefers the first match):

| Installed file | Replaces or adds |
| --- | --- |
| `~/.local/lib/qt6/plugins/plasma/applets/org.kde.plasma.systemtray.so` | the system tray (drag and drop, hidden items, click fixes) |
| `~/.local/lib/qt6/plugins/plasma/applets/org.kde.plasma.notifications.so` | the notifications applet (macOS banners) |
| `~/.local/lib/qt6/plugins/plasma/kcms/kinfocenter/kcm_energyinfo.so` | Info Center > Energy |
| `~/.local/lib/qt6/plugins/org.kde.kdecoration3/org.aurora.decoration.so` | adds the window decoration, chosen in kwinrc |
| `~/.local/lib/qt6/plugins/kwin/plugins/aurora-pointer.so` | adds a KWin plugin: the pointing hand over window buttons |

KWin starts before the login script sets the plugin path, so the decoration and the pointer plugin are also linked
into `/usr/lib/qt6/plugins/` ([install.md](install.md)).

The QML module `org.aurora.glass` (`BlurBehind`, `PointerHints`) lives in `~/.local/lib/qt6/qml/org/aurora/glass`.
plasmashell finds it through `~/.config/systemd/user/plasma-plasmashell.service.d/aurora.conf`, Quick Menu through
its own drop-in.

## Processes started instead of the stock ones

| Override | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `~/.config/systemd/user/plasma-krunner.service.d/aurora.conf` | `plasma-krunner.service` runs `~/.local/lib/aurora/quick-menu/krunner-launch`, which starts Quick Menu when it was built for the installed Plasma and Qt, and `/usr/bin/krunner` otherwise |
| `~/.config/systemd/user/plasma-{kwin_wayland,plasmashell}.service.d/90-aurora-noswap.conf` | `MemorySwapMax=0`: the compositor and the shell never go to swap |
| `~/.local/share/dbus-1/services/org.freedesktop.FileManager1.service` | "Show in folder" opens File Explorer (`--service`) |
| `~/.local/share/dbus-1/services/org.freedesktop.impl.portal.desktop.aurora.service`, `~/.local/share/xdg-desktop-portal/portals/aurora.portal`, `~/.config/xdg-desktop-portal/kde-portals.conf` (`FileChooser=aurora;kde`) | Open and Save panels are File Explorer windows (`--portal`) |
| `~/.config/environment.d/90-aurora-portal.conf` | the portal environment for apps that systemd starts |

## Shortcuts (kglobalaccel, over D-Bus)

- Win+E: Dolphin's `_launch` gives up Meta+E and `file-explorer.desktop` `_launch` takes it (`set_explorer_shortcut`
  in `installer/install.py`).
- Win alone: moved from plasmashell's "Activate Application Launcher" to `org.kde.krunner.desktop` `_launch`
  ([`components/windows-key/windows_key.py`](../components/windows-key/windows_key.py) `quick-menu`). Since Plasma 6.1
  a lone modifier is an ordinary kglobalaccel shortcut; `kwinrc [ModifierOnlyShortcuts]` is no longer read.

## Settings the install writes

Saved first (the `SAVED` list of `installer/install.py`) and put back by the uninstall: `kdeglobals`, `kwinrc`,
`plasmarc`, `kcminputrc`, `dolphinrc`, `konsolerc`, the Plasma panel file, `plasmashellrc`, `kglobalshortcutsrc`,
`mimeapps.list`, `plasmanotifyrc`, `xdg-desktop-portal/kde-portals.conf`, Kvantum, GTK 2/3/4, xsettingsd,
`konsolestaterc`. The notable keys: kwinrc decoration `org.aurora.decoration` with `ButtonsOnRight=IAX`,
`[Windows] ElectricBorderPushbackPixels=0` (one touch of the bottom edge brings the Dock back),
`plasmanotifyrc [Notifications] PopupPosition=BottomRight`, the icon theme `Aurora-dark`, the Konsole
profile `Aurora`, and the panel layout from [`themes/panels/layout.js`](../themes/panels/layout.js).

## Files the install adds to the home folder

The `ADDED` list of `installer/install.py`, removed again by the uninstall through the backup's `created.txt`: the
base icon themes (`Aurora-base`, `Aurora-base-dark`), the `Aurora-dark` icon theme, the `Aurora` cursors (and
`~/.icons/Aurora`), the theme's own app icons, Aurora's color scheme, Plasma style, Kvantum theme and GTK theme, the
Dawn Bird wallpaper, the six
widgets, File Explorer and its desktop entry, the Quick Menu entry, the Konsole profile and toolbars, the plugins and the
glass module above, the login script, the systemd drop-ins, the D-Bus services and the portal, and two state folders:
`~/.local/share/aurora` (what each part was built for, `rebuild.sh`, and `source`, a link to the checkout) and
`~/.local/lib/aurora` (Quick Menu and its launcher).

The backups live in `~/.local/state/aurora/backups/`, with `latest-backup` naming the one the uninstall uses;
they outlive an uninstall.

## Outside the home folder (root)

| File | Purpose | Undo |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/usr/lib/qt6/plugins/org.kde.kdecoration3/org.aurora.decoration.so` (link) | KWin loads the decoration before the session environment | `./uninstall.sh` |
| `/usr/lib/qt6/plugins/kwin/plugins/aurora-pointer.so` (link) | the KWin pointer plugin | `./uninstall.sh` |
| `/etc/scx_loader.toml`, and `scx_loader.service` enabled | scx_lavd in Auto mode at boot (`--performance`) | `./uninstall.sh` |
| `/etc/tmpfiles.d/thp.conf` | THP defrag `defer` (`--performance`) | `./uninstall.sh` |
| `/etc/sysctl.d/99-aurora-memory.conf`, `/etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf.d/90-aurora-zram.conf` | `vm.watermark_scale_factor=125`, zram lz4 (`--performance`) | `./uninstall.sh` |

Why each tuning value: [performance.md](performance.md).

---

Source: docs/components.md (Components)

[Aurora](../README.md) / [Documentation](index.md) / Components

# The components

One section per folder of [`components/`](../components), then the themes. Each says what the part does, where its
source is, what is installed and how it is tested. Build commands are in [build.md](build.md), test commands in
[../tests/index.md](../tests/index.md).

## File Explorer (`components/file-explorer`)

A Finder-style file manager in C++ and Qt Widgets on top of Dolphin's KParts view. A sidebar with Favorites, drives
and color Tags (drives can be renamed inline, kept in `file-explorerrc [Drive Names]`; SF-style symbols; a capacity bar
with a tooltip, amber above 90 % and red above 95 %; a folder the user added unfolds into its subfolders and each
section folds away, kept in `file-explorerrc [Sidebar Tree]`), tabs, a toolbar with an address field
(`fe::AddressField`) that shows the path as clickable segments and takes a typed path on a click beside them, Ctrl+L or
Alt+D (rules in `core/address`: `~`, relative paths, suggestions, shell Tab) and the Group, Share
(Purpose), Edit Tags and More menus, a row of file actions (`fe::ActionBar`), Quick Look (`fe::QuickLook`, Space;
rules in `core/quicklook`), Split View (`fe::TabPage`, F3), a path bar that names the selected file and shows the item
count, Undo (Ctrl+Z) from KIO's undo history, which Dolphin's view records its operations in, a filter row
(`fe::FilterBar`, Ctrl+Alt+F or More > Filter by Name) that keeps the items whose names contain what is typed, case
ignored, with the count of matches, and ends when the tab shows another folder or search, a Rename sheet for several
items (`fe::BatchRenameSheet`, F2 with more than one item selected; rules in `core/batchrename`: replace text or a
regular expression, add text, a name with an index, a counter or each item's date, a change of case; extensions kept
the way KIO keeps them) that shows every new name, marks the ones that cannot be taken and why, plans again against
the folders when Rename is pressed, and runs one KIO batch job that one Undo takes back, a command palette (`fe::CommandPalette`, Ctrl+Shift+P or
More > Command Palette; ranking in `core/palette`: letters in order, word starts and runs count more) that lists every
command of the menus, refreshed for the tab on screen, with its menu and its shortcut, Copy Path (Ctrl+Alt+C, `fe::BrowserTab::copyPaths`, rules in `core/paths`) that
copies every selected item's path, one per line, or the folder's path when nothing is selected (Dolphin copies the
first item only), the Inspector (`fe::InspectorPanel`, Ctrl+Alt+I or View > Show Inspector, remembered in
`file-explorerrc [Inspector]`; rules in `core/inspector`) at the right of the files: a preview, the kind, the real
size of folders and selections (counted like `du` on a thread at idle CPU and I/O priority: one filesystem, links not
followed, hard links once, on-disk size beside it, unreadable folders named) counted again when the folder's own
listing changes, where it is, its dates, owner and permissions, and for a file its SHA-256, SHA-512, SHA-1 or MD5 on
request with a field that compares a pasted hash or `sha256sum` line; hidden, it watches and runs nothing (a folder in an archive or on another machine is read and counted through KIO),
archives as folders (`fe::BrowserTab::archiveFolderUrl`, View > Open Archives as Folders, on by default in
`file-explorerrc [General] ArchivesAsFolders`: a double click opens a zip, tar or 7z through kio-extras' archive worker,
as Windows' File Explorer opens a zip; OpenDocument and other zip-based documents still open in their applications;
the path reads as the archive's own path, then the folders in it, and Up from its top opens its folder with the
archive selected), Git (Dolphin's Git plugin from `dolphin-plugins`, which the installer turns on in `dolphinrc
[VersionControl] enabledPlugins` without turning off the user's others: each file in a repository shows its status,
and the context menu has a Git submenu with Log, Add, Commit, Push and the rest, taken from the part's action groups
by `fe::BrowserTab::versionControlActions`), smart folders (Save at the right of the search row names the search
and puts it in Favorites as a KDE place, so Dolphin lists it under Search For; it opens like a folder, its icon a
magnifier, and the index's change notices keep it current), a columns view (`fe::ColumnsStrip`, the fourth view button, View > as
Columns, remembered in `file-explorerrc [View] Columns`; which folders in `core/paths` `columnFolders`: a column per
folder from home, or from the disk's root, to the folder on screen, each a KIO listing kept current, with Dolphin's list
as the last column, so every file action stays Dolphin's; a click on a folder opens it, on a file opens its folder
with it selected, and files dropped on a column's folder go into it), path segments in both bars (`fe::CrumbStrip`, rules in `core/crumbs`; below), Finder menus with shortcuts written the Windows way (`fe::shortcutLabel`: "Ctrl+Alt+C", "Alt+Enter", "Win+E"),
and the pointing hand on every clickable widget.

Group offers the Finder's choices (None, Name, Kind, Date Modified, Date Created, Size, Tags) through Dolphin's own
actions: `group_by_none` and `group_<role>` since Dolphin 26.08, which groups apart from the sort order and remembers
the choice per folder, and `show_in_groups` with the sort column before it. The toolbar's fields draw one capsule
focus ring (`style::paintFocusRing`); `FinderStyle` drops the `QFocusFrame` Breeze adds around a field focused by Tab
or a shortcut. The window is glass with KWin's blur while it is active and opaque while it is not, as macOS materials
are when their window is not key, so nothing behind shows through it whether KWin blurs or not; selections turn gray
with it.

The address field and the path bar show the path as segments (`fe::CrumbStrip`, which each bar feeds its events;
the layout, the hit test and the drop rules are pure functions in `core/crumbs`, tested). The address field shows them
at rest without icons, as Windows' address bar does, and opens for typing on a click beside them, Ctrl+L or Alt+D (its
focus policy is Tab, so a click on a segment opens the folder instead of the field). A click opens a segment and a
middle click or Ctrl+click opens it in a background tab; the chevron after a segment lists its visible folders (250 at
most, the next one of the path in bold, then Show All); a path too long for its bar folds the segments after the
first into an ellipsis, outermost first, which lists them, and the folder on screen keeps the rest of the room; a
right-click offers Open, Open in New Tab, Open Terminal Here, Copy Path and Get Info. Files dropped on a segment go
through `KIO::drop`, as on the sidebar, so KIO asks Move, Copy or Link; a tag's shelf tags them instead. Refused: a
folder into itself or a folder inside it, files into the folder they are in, Recents, a search, Network, the shelf
of all tags, a folder that is not writable, and the selected file the path bar can end with. A drag resting 700 ms on
a segment opens it (Finder's spring-loaded folders), except the folder on screen. A segment dragged out carries its
URL. The tooltip of a segment is its whole path. Screen readers see the path bar as a group of links, one per segment,
which they can press (`crumbaccessible.cpp`); the address field is a line edit whose text is the whole path. KIO opens
its Move, Copy or Link menu at the drop's position mapped from the widget given to `KJobWidgets::setWindow`
(`src/widgets/dropjob.cpp`, v6.31.0, line 671), so a drop names the widget whose coordinates the drop has: the bar,
or the sidebar's viewport.

Search answers from aurora-search's index of every local disk when it runs ([search.md](search.md)): a KIO worker
(`src/plugins/searchworker.cpp`, `aurora-search:` URLs) lists the helper's matches into Dolphin's view, so they have
icons, columns, drag and drop and menus; `fe::SearchService` keeps one connection while a window is in use, which
keeps the helper and its live updates running, and lets go after three idle minutes; a scope row under the toolbar
(`fe::SearchScopeBar`) chooses This PC or the folder, kept in `file-explorerrc [Search] Everywhere`; hidden names are
matched only while the view shows hidden files. A folder the index does not hold (a network share, a phone) is
searched in place with Dolphin's filenamesearch, as before.

Color tags (`tagging.cpp`, rules in `core/tags`) live in the file's `user.xdg.tags` attribute through KFileMetaData, so
Dolphin and Baloo read them too. Each tag's sidebar row opens its shelf, `~/.local/share/file-explorer/tags/<Tag>`, a
folder of links to the tagged files that File Explorer keeps in step and tidies as it opens, so tags work without
Baloo's index. The `aurora-tags` KIO overlay plugin (`src/plugins`, installed in
`~/.local/lib/qt6/plugins/kf6/overlayicon`) draws a tagged file's colors as dots on its icon, in File Explorer and in
Dolphin, with the 63 emblems `themes/icons/tag_emblems.py` adds to the icon theme.

It also serves `org.freedesktop.FileManager1` (`--service`: "Show in folder" selects the file) and the FileChooser
portal backend (`--portal`: Open and Save panels with a chooser bar; it quits after three idle minutes). Installed as
`~/.local/bin/file-explorer`; Win+E launches it. Folders without a view of their own show Finder's columns (Name,
Modified, Size, Type) from `~/.local/share/file-explorer/view_properties/global/.directory`. Tests: `fe_tests` (90),
`fe_finder_tests` (55), `fe_widget_tests` (24, offscreen: clicks, drops, a drag resting on a segment, the address
field at rest, accessibility, the filter row over a real Dolphin view, the glass behind a field inside a tab, the
Rename sheet renaming a real folder and one Undo taking it back, F2 on two items opening it, the command palette
finding, running and closing, Copy Path with three items and with none, the Inspector counting a
folder and again after a change, hashing a file and comparing a pasted hash, a tar.gz opened as a
folder, Up out of it, the Inspector counting inside it, the search row's Save and its folder capsule hidden when the index
does not hold the folder, the columns leading to a folder and opening
what is clicked), `tests/installer/test_tag_emblems.sh` (5). Sandbox: `explorer.sh`, `explorer-crumbs.sh` (the path
segments: hover, both menus, a drop in the accent, a segment opening under a drag, KIO's menu at the pointer on a
segment and on the sidebar, a refused drop, Ctrl+L, Ctrl+click and middle click), `explorer-finder.sh` (the
mockup's scene: tags, the unfolded sidebar, the menu, a typed path, Quick Look, Split View, a tag's shelf, the Group
menu and the folder grouped by Kind from it, and the window inactive behind another),
`explorer-menus.sh`, `explorer-drives.sh`, `explorer-search.sh` (search from the index: whole home, scope row, hidden
names, Save to a smart folder in Favorites and opening it), `explorer-undo.sh` (Delete, then Ctrl+Z brings the file back; FAIL on the code before Undo), `explorer-filter.sh`
(Ctrl+Alt+F, a word hides the rest, no match empties the view, Escape brings everything back), `explorer-rename.sh`
(Ctrl+A, F2, find and replace, Enter, then Ctrl+Z; 3 PASS), `explorer-palette.sh` (Ctrl+Shift+P, "show hidden",
Enter; 3 PASS), `explorer-copypaths.sh` (Ctrl+A, Ctrl+Alt+C, the three paths read
from Klipper and pasted into KWrite), `explorer-inspector.sh` (Ctrl+Alt+I on a
folder, a picture, Compute and a typed SHA-256 that matches; 3 PASS), `explorer-archive.sh` (a double click on a
zip, then Alt+Up; 2 PASS), `explorer-git.sh` (a repository's
status emblems, the context menu and its Git submenu; needs `dolphin-plugins` or `AURORA_DOLPHIN_PLUGINS` naming its
unpacked package; 2 PASS), `explorer-columns.sh` (the
columns view from the palette, a click in a column; 2 PASS), `show-in-folder.sh`, `open-save.sh`.

## Mission Center (`components/mission-center`)

Mission Center, the system monitor, built from upstream main with Aurora's patches: each app's GPU and memory counted
exactly (memory as PSS; the sum came within 0.4 % of the real total on my own machine), magpie kept lean (3 % of one
core with the window open and 0.6 % hidden, against 13 % for Mission Center 1.2.0), fans read the way the hardware
reports them, each app's network use from nethogs, a color per device in the sidebar, and smoother graphs. The folder
holds the package's recipe: the `PKGBUILD` (package `mission-center-improved`, in place of the distribution's
`mission-center`), one patch per upstream repository, a pacman hook that gives nethogs the two capabilities it needs
to count traffic without root, and an install script that takes them away with the package. `make_patches.sh` writes
the patches from the four upstream clones the work is done in, which stay next to it and out of git.

The look matches File Explorer's glass (`resources/ui/aurora.css` for the window, `aurora-header.css` for the header
bars, `aurora-pages.css` for the pages and `aurora-popups.css` for what opens over them, in light and dark style
alike, as Aurora's GTK theme is dark in both),
measured over the same wallpaper as File Explorer in the sandbox. `src/glass.rs` paints File Explorer's tint,
rgba(24, 24, 27, 0.63), over the window body but for the sidebar's card, which stays the clearer glass on its own
(`paint_tint`, as File Explorer's `glassCutout`, drawn as the card's shadow with no blur so no path is rasterized);
GTK's own window background stays clear, since the GTK theme fills it at 96 %. KWin blurs behind it, and the window
turns the blur off while it is not in front and opaque, as File Explorer does: `glass.rs` asks through
ext-background-effect-v1 itself, once per size or state (KWin 6.8 removed Plasma's `org_kde_kwin_blur`, which it
still uses where the new protocol is missing). A surface may hold one effect object and GTK 4.24 makes one for every
surface, so `main` keeps GDK off the protocol with `GDK_WAYLAND_DISABLE` (tested). GTK's own way, CSS
`backdrop-filter`, built copy, paste and blur nodes into every frame and walked the whole frame for the region: with
animated graphs the window used 66 % of a core instead of 20 % ([performance.md](performance.md)). KWin 6.8 places
the region from the window's edge rather than the surface's, so GTK's client-side shadow put the blur 68 by 50 px
off; the window is
undecorated instead, KWin draws File Explorer's shadow (`src/shadow.rs`, `org_kde_kwin_shadow`, tests on the image and
its tiles) and the window resizes from a 6 px band inside its edges (`src/edges.rs`, tested). `glass.rs` loads the
four sheets one step above the user's sheet (`~/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css`): a desktop theme loaded there outranks every
app's own sheet, and its generic row and button rules turned the selected row grey and the selected device solid
blue. The header row is File Explorer's
toolbar, measured on both apps' captures: 34 px capsules 15 px below the window's top, the window buttons in File
Explorer's 120 by 34 px capsule 22 px in from the right edge with the same glyphs, round buttons of 34 px, 18 px
symbols, File Explorer's fills and rim, and a search field of 230 px that narrows to 150 px when the header is short of
room (below 1220 scaled pixels, or while the sidebar is edited) so the page switcher keeps its labels. The sidebar's
header is File Explorer's too: its sidebar button (File Explorer's symbol) and the Edit button at the top left, the
edit tools at the other end while editing; with the sidebar hidden, the header bar's sidebar button takes the same
place, and a window in the background keeps its header as it is but for the window buttons' glyphs. The device sidebar
is the clearer glass, 6 px from the window's edges; each device's pill keeps 8 px from the card's sides and its graph
10 px from the pill's edge, as File Explorer's rows do. The tables and the Performance graphs start 25 px from the
sidebar and end 16 px above the window's bottom edge and, like the details column, 22 px from its right edge, under
the window buttons. The sidebar stays on every page; on Apps and Services it shows from 1220
scaled pixels, where every column still fits (measured: the Apps table needs 871 px with a process tree ten levels
deep, the sidebar and margins 328).
Apps and Services put their table on a glass card with the column headings inside; section headings (Apps,
Processes) never show as selected; Stop, Force Stop, Details, Start and Restart are separate glass pills. A heading
keeps no room for the sort arrow until its column is sorted, reading columns are 64 px at least (75 upstream) and each
tree level steps in 16 px (22 in the theme), which together let the table fit beside the sidebar. Busy cells get a
rounded heat tint (`src/table_view/columns/heat.rs`, five steps per unit, accent blue for CPU and GPU shares and amber
for memory and throughput, tested; setting `apps-page-heat-tint`). On Performance, `src/performance_page/tiles.rs`
turns each device's readings into glass tiles (two to a row where the layout allows) with the facts on one card below,
lined up with the top of the graphs; it reads the shape of each device's layout file, so every device gets the same
look (tests on what counts as a reading, the facts' span and the pairing). A network's addresses are facts on the same
card. A drive's partitions sit on a card of their own under the facts and as wide as theirs, under File Explorer's
section title (11 px, semibold, secondary); each mount point shows a folder symbol, and each usage bar is File
Explorer's capacity bar, blue, amber past 90 % used and red past 95 % (its thresholds, tested). The details column
takes about a third of the page and is never narrower than its tiles; in a narrow window the graphs give way instead.
The search field is always in the header bar. Graph corners stay at the stock 7 px: at 10 and 12 GTK 4.24's
GPU renderer logged clip errors.
Menus are File Explorer's (`aurora-popups.css`, from its `finderstyle.cpp`): glass 11 px round and at least 180 px
wide, 24 px rows with the text 14 px in, an accent pill under the pointer or the keyboard but none on the first row
when a menu opens with the mouse, an 18 px column with a check mark on the chosen choice, secondary shortcuts and
chevrons, and hairlines between sections. Submenus open beside their menu (`flags: nested`) instead of sliding in, and
no menu has a tail. Tooltips are the same glass, 8 px round. KWin blurs behind each of them and draws their shadow:
`src/popups.rs` gives every popover and tooltip, as it maps, its own blur, fitted to its size as GTK lays it out, and
File Explorer's menu shadow, those GTK makes on its own included (submenus, the search field's menu), through an
emission hook on GtkWidget's `map`. Over a checkerboard in the sandbox, a shadow drawn by GTK widened the menu's surface and KWin put the blur off
by the shadow's reach, as it did for the window. Dialogs are opaque in File Explorer's dialog color, rgb(30, 30, 32),
with the window's rim, and their grouped rows sit on one card; Preferences is 820 px wide so its four page names fit
(at 640 the switcher, which gives every page the room of the longest name, Performance Page, cut them short).
The sandbox (`tools/sandbox`) captures over Aurora's wallpaper, or another picture with `MC_BACKDROP`, with the host's
icons, fonts, icon theme, font setting and whole `~/.config/gtk-4.0`, at any width (`MC_WIDTH`) and style
(`MC_STYLE`), and can click a spot first (`click+X+Y`), leave the pointer over one (`hover+X+Y`) or play any input
(`input+WORDS`, fakeinput's words, such as a right-click and a move into the menu it opens).

`aurora mission-center on` installs it from Aurora's repository when pacman finds it there, otherwise it builds it
here with makepkg (about ten minutes; the build tools come and go with `--syncdeps --rmdeps`); `off` puts the
distribution's back. Every change first saves a snapshot in `~/.local/state/aurora/mission-center/snapshots/<time>`
(which build was installed, and `dconf dump` of the settings), and every build Aurora installs is kept in
`~/.local/state/aurora/mission-center/packages`, so `rollback [NAME]` puts both back; `snapshots` lists them. pacman's
own snapshots (snap-pac) cover the system side. `settings` offers the refresh, the points on each chart, the look,
smooth and sliding graphs, one row per app, kernel time, fans and batteries, and resets the sidebar's order and the
device colors; `--set KEY=VALUE` and `--reset KEY` reach every key of `io.missioncenter.MissionCenter`, each value
checked against `gsettings range` before anything changes. Tests: the CLI's `mission` tests and the contract test on
the recipe ([../tests/index.md](../tests/index.md)).

## Window buttons (`components/window-buttons`)

The KDecoration3 plugin `org.aurora.decoration` ("Aurora" in System Settings): one glass capsule with
minimize, maximize and close in Windows order, the same size as the GTK and File Explorer buttons. `deco-preview`
renders it offscreen. Tests: `decoration_tests` (11). KWin loads it through a root link (it starts before the session's
plugin path is set); the login script pauses it when KDecoration changes.

## System tray (`components/system-tray`)

Plasma 6.8.2's tray applet with `system-tray.patch`: Windows 11 drag and drop (reorder, drop on the arrow to hide),
working clicks on app icons, SF-like status icons (from `themes/icons/status_glyphs.py`). The items behind the arrow
are set by `themes/panels/tray_hide.py` while plasmashell is stopped. Tests: `tests/tst_draglayering.qml` (5).
Sandbox: `tray-click.sh`, `tray-drag.sh`, `tray-show.sh`.

## Notifications (`components/notifications`)

Plasma 6.8.2's notifications applet with `notifications.patch`: macOS banners (356 px wide, a radius of about 22, the
Control Center's glass shader, the app icon leading, a bold title, "now" in the trailing corner, four lines of body, a
close button on hover over the top-left corner, the button shared with the popover in `components/BannerButton.qml`),
in the bottom-right corner (`PopupPosition=BottomRight`), 8 px apart. The popover (`FullRepresentation.qml`) keeps
Plasma's history and every control, drawn as macOS Tahoe's Notification Center: each notification is a glass platter
inset from the edges with the banner's layout (`DelegatePopup`, dates past 22 hours), a long body folded to four
lines that a click or Show More opens, Clear on hover over its top-right corner (the time fades under it), and the
app's settings, Minimize and Close in a right-click or Menu-key menu; a group is its app's icon and name above its
platters; Do not disturb is a row with the switch trailing; the empty
state is a bell with "No Notifications". SwipeDelegate moves its background with the swipe and ignores insets, so the
platter is inset inside a full-width background item.
The window asks for a theme frame that does not exist (`aurora/no-frame`), so Plasma draws no frame of its own, and
an `inputRect` mask lets clicks through the shadow margin. The project needs `LANGUAGES C` for the generated Wayland
protocol code; `plasma-shell.xml` is kept in `vendor/protocols`. Sandbox: `notifications.sh`,
`notifications-history.sh` (the popover with notifications, on hover, empty with `SCEN_TAG=empty`, a group with
`SCEN_TAG=group`; Plasma keeps an expired notification only when it names its desktop entry).

## Quick Menu (`components/quick-menu`)

KRunner from plasma-workspace 6.8.2 (`upstream/`, `vendor/`, `quick-menu.patch`) drawn as macOS Tahoe's Spotlight: one
frameless glass window floating a quarter of the way down the active screen. With nothing typed it shows the
Applications view: Suggestions (the apps used most, from Plasma's activity statistics through Kicker's
`RecentUsageModel`) and Plasma's menu in Tahoe's sections (`quickmenu.js`: categories keyed by their `.directory`
icon, merged, de-duplicated, sorted), one row of five per section until "Show More". The grid button beside ⋯ in the search
row opens All Applications: every app once under its first letter, accents filed under the plain letter and digits and signs under "#" first
(`alphabeticalSections()`, like Windows' All apps), under a heading drawn like a section's with Back where a
section has Show More; the button, filled while the list shows, also goes back. The arrow keys walk the grid, the
pointer selects only when it really moves, Return launches. An app dragged onto another of its section takes that
app's place, and the section keeps that order (`~/.config/aurora/quick-menu.conf`; Suggestions stay ordered by
use). A right-click on an app, or the Menu key or Shift+F10 on the selected one, opens its menu (`QuickMenuPopup.qml`,
built by `quickmenu.js` `menuItems()`): Open, the app's jump list, Pin to Top (a Pinned section above Suggestions,
saved in `quick-menu.conf`), Pin to Dock (the Dock's launchers, changed through Plasma's `evaluateScript` with a script
that accepts only a desktop file id), Remove from Suggestions (Kicker's `forget`), then Plasma's Edit Application and
Uninstall. Plasma's own pin actions are left out: Kicker offers them only inside a panel widget. Typing searches
everything KRunner's runners find, listed
with their actions, drag-out and section headers; Up in the empty field recalls past searches. The ⋯ menu keeps Keep
Open, Usage Help and KRunner's settings. It starts through `krunner-launch.sh` and the `plasma-krunner` drop-in
([architecture.md](architecture.md)); the menu bar's search icon calls `org.kde.krunner /App toggleDisplay`. Tests:
`tests/tst_quickmenu.qml` (43), `tests/test_launch.sh` (5). Sandbox: `quick-menu.sh`, `quick-menu-all.sh`, `quick-menu-drag.sh`,
`quick-menu-app-menu.sh`.

## The Windows key (`components/windows-key`)

`windows_key.py quick-menu|stock|status` moves `Qt::Key_Meta` (16777250) between plasmashell's "Activate Application
Launcher" (which keeps Alt+F1) and KRunner's `_launch` over kglobalaccel's D-Bus API, leaving every other key alone. Win
alone opens Quick Menu, the next press closes it, Win+key combinations are untouched. Sandbox: `windows-key.sh` (the
first check reproduces the old bug, then four PASS).

## Control Center (`components/control-center`)

The widget `org.aurora.controlcenter`, Tahoe's floating glass modules: Wi-Fi or Ethernet, Bluetooth, Focus, sound with a device panel, the player,
Night Light, screen mirroring, settings and screenshots. The blur comes from `org.aurora.glass`. Tests: `tests/tst_cc.qml` (20). Sandbox: `control-center*.sh`.

## Glass and pointer hints (`components/glass`)

The C++ QML module `org.aurora.glass`. `BlurBehind` asks KWin to blur behind rounded items marked
`glassBlur: true`; `PointerHints` gives plasmashell the pointing hand over clickable items (an application event filter
with a top-down item search like Qt's own delivery, loaded once by the Control Center). Quick Menu and the banners use
the blur too. Tests: `tests/tst_blurbehind.qml` (9), `tests/tst_pointerhints.qml` (13). Sandbox: `pointing-hand.sh`,
`pointing-hand-cost.sh`.

## Pointing hand over window buttons (`components/pointing-hand`)

The KWin plugin `aurora-pointer` shows the hand over buttons that KWin draws (an `InputEventSpy` and
`Cursor::setSource`, no KWin patch). KWin loads it through a root link and refuses it after a KWin version change until
`rebuild.sh` runs. Sandbox: `pointing-hand-kwin.sh`.

## Logo menu (`components/kali-menu`)

The widget `org.aurora.logomenu`: the menu behind the menu bar's logo (CachyOS, Arch Linux, Apple or the Kali dragon),
with shortcut labels written the Windows way. The labels
are the menu's own accelerators while it is open ("Ctrl+Alt+Q" locks, "Alt+Shift+Q" logs out). Tests:
`tests/tst_menu.qml` (31 pass; `test_mouse_drag_reorders` is a known failure). Sandbox:
`kali-menu.sh`.

## Clock (`components/clock`) and Dock divider (`components/dock-divider`)

`org.aurora.clock` writes the date and time the way macOS does ("Wed Nov 4  6:24 PM", in the system's language)
with a calendar popup; tests: `tests/tst_clock.qml` (9). `org.aurora.dockdivider` is the thin line between the apps
and the stacks in the Dock.

## Info Center energy page (`components/energy-page`)

A KCM with the stock id `kcm_energyinfo`: live CPU package watts (RAPL), GPU watts and temperature (NVML through dlopen),
a two-minute chart and the power profile buttons (power-profiles-daemon over D-Bus); it samples only while visible.
Tests: `test_power` (9). Sandbox: `energy-page.sh`.

## Menu bar and Dock layout (`themes/panels`)

`layout.js` is a Plasma desktop script: the menu bar (menu bar style, logo menu, app name, spacer, tray, Quick Menu,
Control Center, clock; translucent, because an adaptive bar turns opaque over a maximized window and its popups with
it) and the Dock (task manager with the pinned apps carried over, divider, Downloads, Trash).
`render_layout.sh` fills its placeholders: the home folder and the three gaps that keep the right-hand icons 46 px
apart, as the tray's own icons are. A placeholder is a name in capitals between two `@`; the installer stops when
one is left, and any other `@` is the script's own text. `patch_tray.py` copies the tray settings from the backup; `tray_hide.py` puts
Brightness, Clipboard, Disks and Bluetooth behind the arrow. Sandbox: `setup-panels.sh`, `menu-bar.sh`,
`dock-keeps-pins.sh`, `dock.sh`, `dock-edge.sh`.

## Menu bar style and app name (`components/menu-bar-style`, `components/app-title`)

`org.aurora.menubarstyle` gives the menu bar its light text, soft shadow and spacing; it stays hidden in the bar.
`org.aurora.apptitle` names the active app in bold next to the logo, and takes no room when no window has the focus.
Tests: `components/app-title/tests/tst_apptitle.qml`. Sandbox: `app-title.sh`.

## Themes, icons, fonts (`themes/`)

- Dawn Bird, Aurora's own wallpaper, a Plasma wallpaper package in `themes/wallpapers/Aurora` (5120x2880 and
  3840x2160, CC BY-SA 4.0); the README's pictures and the sandbox's showcase captures are taken on it.
- Aurora's Plasma style (`themes/plasma/Aurora`; its top panel stays see-through), color scheme
  (`themes/colors/Aurora.colors`) and Kvantum theme (`themes/kvantum/Aurora`); the GTK theme in
  `themes/gtk/Aurora.tar.xz`, adjusted by `gtk_theme.py` (the window-button capsule for GTK 3, GTK 4 and
  libadwaita, with File Explorer's glyphs written half a pixel off the icon's middle, so each 1.4 px stroke falls on
  one row of pixels as File Explorer and the decoration draw it; the GTK 4 sheet's copy of libadwaita's list header
  padding is narrowed to lists, because the user sheet loads above every app's own and would otherwise pad table
  headings that an app sets itself).
- Icons: the base themes `Aurora-base` and `Aurora-base-dark`, kept built in `themes/icons/base/Aurora-base.tar.xz`
  (hidden in the icon picker), and `Aurora-dark` built at install by `themes/icons/build_icon_theme.py` (each app's
  own logo ahead of the base's redraws), `status_glyphs.py` (SF-like
  status icons, written as filled outlines because GTK 4 fills every shape of a symbolic icon and drops strokes) and the theme's Settings, Downloads and Trash icons in `themes/icons/system` (drawn by
  `draw_system_icons.py`).
- Cursors: `themes/cursors/Aurora`, with four aliases Plasma asks for.
- Fonts: none are shipped. The interface uses Inter (`inter-font`) and Konsole JetBrains Mono with Nerd Fonts' symbols
  (`ttf-jetbrains-mono-nerd`); `install.py` picks SF Pro Text and SF Mono with Nerd symbols instead when the user
  installed them (`ui_font()`, `mono_font()`), since Apple's license forbids redistributing them.
- Konsole: `themes/konsole` (the "Aurora" profile and color scheme, toolbars hidden).

## Measurement kit (`performance/measure`)

`probe.py` (time from a shortcut to its window, plus scheduler wait), `under-load.sh`, `sched/` (scheduler rounds,
`rtlat.c`, results) and `power/` (`ab.sh`, `burst.c`: Balanced against Performance). Results: [performance.md](performance.md).

[Aurora](../README.md) / [Documentation](index.md) / Build

# Building the parts

`./install.sh` builds everything on its own. This page is for building by hand while changing a part.

## Everything

```bash
installer/build.sh                 # every part into build/<part>, with logs in build/<part>.build.log
installer/build.sh quick-menu       # only the parts named
installer/build.sh --plan          # where each Plasma part's sources come from; builds nothing
```

Packages: [`installer/dependencies.txt`](../installer/dependencies.txt) (`./install.sh --check` lists the missing ones).
Every build is CMake with Ninja in `RelWithDebInfo`, through ccache when it is installed, at `nice 10`. A finished
part gets `build/<part>/built-for`, the versions it was built against; the install copies it beside the part.

| Part | Output in `build/` | Built for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| file-explorer | `file-explorer/file-explorer`, `fe_tests` | Qt |
| window-buttons | `window-buttons/org.aurora.decoration.so`, `decoration_tests`, `deco-preview` | KDecoration major.minor |
| glass | `glass/qml/org/aurora/glass/` | Qt |
| energy-page | `energy-page/bin/plasma/kcms/kinfocenter/kcm_energyinfo.so`, `test_power` | Qt |
| pointing-hand | `pointing-hand/aurora-pointer.so` | KWin |
| system-tray | `system-tray/bin/plasma/applets/org.kde.plasma.systemtray.so` | plasma-workspace and Qt |
| notifications | `notifications/bin/plasma/applets/org.kde.plasma.notifications.so` | plasma-workspace and Qt |
| quick-menu | `quick-menu/bin/krunner` | plasma-workspace and Qt |

## The three Plasma parts

The system tray, the notifications and Quick Menu are Plasma's own code. Each component keeps three things:

- `upstream/`: Plasma's files of the version in `vendor/`, untouched;
- `vendor/`: the same files with the theme's changes, the copy that builds;
- `<part>.patch`: the difference between the two (it reproduces `vendor/` exactly from `upstream/`, plus the binary
  `glass.frag.qsb` shader, which is copied).

`build.sh` builds from `vendor/` when the installed plasma-workspace is that version. For any other version it clones
that version's tag from KDE (`git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse`, only the folders the part needs), applies
the patch and builds from there. If the patch no longer applies, the part is skipped and Plasma keeps its own;
[update.md](update.md) shows how to port the patch.

## One part by hand

```bash
cmake -S components/window-buttons -B build/window-buttons -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo
cmake --build build/window-buttons
python3 -I installer/install.py components     # installs every built part, beside what it was built for
```

## Test helpers

```bash
gcc -O2 tests/helpers/fakeinput/fakeinput.c tests/helpers/fakeinput/fake-input-protocol.c -lwayland-client -lm \
    -o tests/helpers/fakeinput/fakeinput
cmake -S tests/helpers/fake-tray -B tests/helpers/fake-tray/build -G Ninja && cmake --build tests/helpers/fake-tray/build
gcc -O2 performance/measure/power/burst.c -o performance/measure/power/burst
```
